source.title: Open Problems on Configuration Spaces of Tensegrities

accepted.question_text: Describe the combinatorics of the three tensegrity configuration spaces B_2(K_6), B_3(K_4), and B_3(K_5), where B_d(G) denotes the configuration space of all realizations of the graph G on labeled vertices in R^d and the stratification is by maximal connected components with equivalent self-stress fibers.

evidence.quote: Denote by B_d(G) = (R^d)^n the configuration space of all tensegrity frameworks.
A stratum is by definition a maximal connected component of B_d(G) with equivalent fibers.
Problem 1 Describe the combinatorics of B_2(K_6), B_3(K_4) and B_3(K_5).

accepted.question_text: In the planar case of tensegrities on 10 labeled points, describe every possible type of stratum that can occur in the configuration-space stratification by sign-preserving equivalence classes of self-stress fibers.

evidence.quote: A stratum is by definition a maximal connected component of B_d(G) with equivalent fibers.
The next case which contains unknown strata is n = 10 (see also Problem 8 below). Problem 2 Describe all the possible different types of strata for 10 points.

accepted.question_text: Determine, as a function of n, how many different types of strata can occur in tensegrity configuration spaces on n labeled points.
accepted.context_brief: Count of stratum types for arbitrary n

evidence.quote: A stratum is by definition a maximal connected component of B_d(G) with equivalent fibers.
Problem 3 Compute the number of different types of strata for n points with arbitrary n.

accepted.question_text: Determine which subgraphs of the complete graph K_n induce exactly the same stratification of tensegrity configuration space.
accepted.context_brief: When subgraphs share the same stratification

evidence.quote: A stratum is by definition a maximal connected component of B_d(G) with equivalent fibers.
In many cases the strata for different graphs coincide. So it is natural to ask the following question. Problem 4 Which subgraphs of Kn define the same stratifications?

accepted.question_text: Find all strata of codimension greater than 1 that cannot be obtained as intersections of closures of several codimension-1 strata in the configuration-space stratification of tensegrities.
accepted.context_brief: Higher-codimension strata not built from codimension one

evidence.quote: A stratum is by definition a maximal connected component of B_d(G) with equivalent fibers.
Problem 5 Find all strata of codimension more than 1 that are not defined as an intersection of the closure of several codimension 1 strata.

accepted.question_text: In the planar Cayley-algebra description of tensegrity strata, determine when two Cayley algebra systems define the same stratum or the same stratum condition; here the Cayley-algebra setting uses points and lines in the plane together with the join and meet operations to express geometric conditions.

Therefore, there are 60 different Cayley algebra systems defining the same stratum. This lead to the following important open problem. Problem 6 Which Cayley algebra systems define the same strata?

accepted.question_text: Given a graph G, determine whether there exists one Cayley algebra system, or several such systems, that describes exactly the union of the codimension-1 tensegrity strata in the plane; equivalently, the union of the codimension-1 strata of B_2(K_n). Here a Cayley algebra system means a description built from planar points and lines using join and meet operations.
accepted.context_brief: Cayley description of all planar codimension-one strata

evidence.quote: Recall that the objects of (planar) Cayley algebra are points and lines in the plane. Cayley algebra has two major operations:

Problem 7 Given a graph G. Does there exist a Cayley algebra system (or several systems) describing the union of the codimension 1 tensegrity strata in the plane [i.e., the union of the codimension 1 strata of B_2(K_n)]?

accepted.question_text: Develop a theory of geometric conditions that define or characterize strata for tensegrities in multidimensional Euclidean spaces, beyond the planar case.

evidence.quote: There is almost nothing known in multidimensional case. Problem 9 Develop theory of geometric conditions for strata in multidimensional case.
